Attached is our Oxbridge v2 questionnaire with a few items we want to confirm in writing before contract sign: specifically Q12–Q16 about where customer prompts and model outputs are stored, deletion guarantees, backups/snapshots, and how ephemeral in-memory caches are handled for hosted deployments.

Top asks:

- Please describe KV cache behavior — is any user content written to disk?

We have a compliance deadline next week, so a concise playbook-style answer would be great (we can iterate after). I attached the questionnaire and your earlier data-flow diagram for reference.

Alice — thanks for the clear list. Below is a short, playbook-style response we can rely on for the questionnaire; I’ve kept each answer concise and included expected timelines. I attached our internal 'erase-playbook' excerpt and the data-flow diagram (redwood_data-flow-diagram.png) for evidence. Happy to expand any item.

1) Default retention (hosted API)
- Default: request and response payloads (raw prompts + model outputs) are retained for 30 days for monitoring, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation. Retention is counted from ingestion timestamp.
- Opt-out / Ephemeral Mode: Customers can enable Ephemeral Mode at onboarding or per-project. In Ephemeral Mode we do not persist request/response payloads to durable object storage; data is only processed in-memory and dropped immediately after tokenization + model response is produced. Ephemeral Mode = 0-day durable retention.

2) Immediate erasure workflow and timelines
- Customer-initiated deletion via the Redwood Delete API or Support request: we remove entries from primary user-visible stores (indexes, object storage, and product logs) immediately (within minutes) and return a deletion confirmation.
- Background purge to backups/snapshots: durable backups and snapshot replicas are deleted according to backup windows. Typical timeline: snapshots are rotated daily and backups are retained for up to 60 days; when a deletion is requested, we mark affected objects for early purge and they are removed from backups within 45 days maximum in 99% of cases. Certain cross-region cold archives may take up to 90 days to fully expire depending on provider retention policies — we document this in the attached playbook.

3) Derivatives (embeddings, indexes, reranks)
- Embeddings and any derived artifacts created by Redwood (e.g., embeddings we generate on behalf of customers) are treated as customer data. They are stored in customer-scoped object stores and indexing services and are deleted by the same Delete API workflow. If Ephemeral Mode is enabled, we do not persist embeddings unless explicitly requested by the customer.

4) KV cache and runtime caches
- KV caches used to speed inference are in-memory on GPU nodes and are not written to disk. They are session-scoped and cleared at session termination. We do not persist KV contents to long-term storage unless an explicit durability flag is set by the customer’s configuration.

5) Backups, snapshots, and forensics
- For customers requiring shorter backup windows we offer a Backup SLA add-on (contractual) that shortens snapshot retention to 30 days and adds an attestation of deletion within 60 days for archived copies. For high-compliance customers we can provide a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) where the customer controls backup lifecycle entirely.

6) Evidence and attestation
- We can provide: an invoice-level export showing data deletion confirmations, a redacted audit log of purge jobs (timestamped), and our erase-playbook document (attached). For SOC 2 or external audits we will coordinate an evidence package on request.

7) Representative statement you can quote in the questionnaire
- "Redwood Inference processes hosted API requests with a default 30-day retention. Customers may enable Ephemeral Mode for zero durable retention. Deletion requests remove data from primary systems immediately; durable backups are removed within defined backup-retention windows (standard: up to 60 days; expedited options available). KV/runtime caches are ephemeral and never written to disk under normal operation."

If this looks good we can sign and return the completed questionnaire. Let me know if Oxbridge needs more aggressive backup purging (Irene can follow up on the Backup SLA contract language).

Best —
Logan Wright
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
